The root cause of the error is that the f-string in the print statement is not properly closed — the line `print(f'Missing data by site:\n{missing_by_site}')` is cut off due to a syntax error in the code cell, likely because of an unescaped newline or malformed string.

Now, I will fix the code by using a regular print with concatenation instead of an f-string to avoid the syntax issue.

function.arguments:
{"code": "import pandas as pd

df = pd.read_csv('/home/musel/Github/research_agent/data/trial.csv')

# Deduplicate: keep highest sample_seq per patient_id
df = df.sort_values('sample_seq', ascending=False).drop_duplicates(subset='patient_id', keep='first')

# Check number of patients with biomarker_baseline = -999
total_missing = len(df[df['biomarker_baseline'] == -999])
missing_df = df[df['biomarker_baseline'] == -999]
responded_missing = missing_df['responded'].sum()
response_rate_missing = responded_missing / total_missing if total_missing > 0 else 0

# Check distribution of missing data across sites
missing_by_site = missing_df['site'].value_counts()

# Compute response rate for each site, including all deduplicated patients (including those with -999)
response_rate_by_site = df.groupby('site')['responded'].mean().round(4)

# Print results
print('Number of patients with biomarker_baseline = -999:', total_missing)
print('Response rate among those with missing baseline:', f'{response_rate_missing:.4f}')
print('Missing data by site:')
print(missing_by_site)
print('Response rates by site (including missing baseline patients):')
print(response_rate_by_site)"}
